title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #8

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What happens to a dead plant? (1 mark)
   A. It flies away
   B. It becomes a rock
   C. It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   D. It turns into an animal

2. What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water? (1 mark)
   A. Make flowers
   B. Make leaves
   C. Carry seeds
   D. Store food

3. What can you use to draw and label a plant if you have a computer at school? (1 mark)
   A. A calculator only
   B. A ruler only
   C. A stopwatch
   D. A drawing app

4. In a seedling, what is the correct order of growth? (1 mark)
   A. Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   B. Leaves, seed, root
   C. Root, flower, seed
   D. Shoot, seed, root

5. Which of these is NOT alive? (1 mark)
   A. A grass blade
   B. A plastic flower
   C. A young mango tree
   D. A maize plant

6. What are the two main types of things carried by the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Heat and cold
   B. Air and stones
   C. Water and food
   D. Sound and light

7. Why do animals need to feed? (1 mark)
   A. To make their skin colourful
   B. To grow feathers only
   C. To get energy and to grow
   D. To make noise

8. Which of these is an insect? (1 mark)
   A. Butterfly
   B. Earthworm
   C. Snail
   D. Crab

9. How many legs does a spider have? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Four
   C. Ten
   D. Eight

10. Which of these animals gives birth to live young? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Frog
   D. Housefly

11. Which of these is NOT a part of the digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Lungs
   B. Gullet
   C. Stomach
   D. Rectum

12. What should you do when you have a persistent stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Tell an adult and see a health worker
   C. Eat more sweets
   D. Drink dirty water

13. A cup can hold about (1 mark)
   A. 25 litres
   B. 25 ml
   C. 2500 ml
   D. 250 ml

14. Which of these can be poured and takes the shape of its container? (1 mark)
   A. Book
   B. Brick
   C. Water
   D. Stone

15. Which of these can be a solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Book
   C. Wooden chair
   D. Stone

16. Which of these is a gas? (1 mark)
   A. Water in a cup
   B. The air in a balloon
   C. A wooden spoon
   D. Flour

17. Which of these is NOT matter? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Air
   C. A stone
   D. Light from a torch

18. Which state of matter is used in a cooking gas cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Powder
   C. Ice
   D. Solid

19. Which of these is a reason we need gases? (1 mark)
   A. We breathe air
   B. We can build houses with them
   C. We can sit on them
   D. We can write with them

20. What is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Anything that makes sound
   B. Anything that is hot
   C. Anything that shines
   D. Anything that has mass and takes up space

21. Which of these breaks down and rots easily? (1 mark)
   A. Glass bottle
   B. Tin can
   C. Plastic bag
   D. Vegetable peelings

22. At a wedding, what can organisers do to keep the place clean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw waste in a river
   B. Burn plastic
   C. Provide bins and clean after the event
   D. Leave waste on the ground

23. Which is an example of reusing? (1 mark)
   A. Using a washed bottle to carry water
   B. Burning a plastic bottle
   C. Throwing it in a drain
   D. Leaving it on the road

24. Why are rotting waste heaps a health danger? (1 mark)
   A. They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   B. They make water sweet
   C. They make soil red
   D. They cool the air

25. How does mulching help save water? (1 mark)
   A. It reduces evaporation from the soil
   B. It makes water flow away
   C. It makes soil hot
   D. It makes soil dry

26. Why is saving water good for families? (1 mark)
   A. It makes water heavier
   B. It reduces the water bill
   C. It stops rain
   D. It causes floods

27. Which of these is a result of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. More trees
   B. More rain
   C. Less water for others
   D. Less money spent

28. Which of these is needed to harvest rainwater from a roof? (1 mark)
   A. A ladder only
   B. A gutter and a tank
   C. A torch
   D. A fan

29. Which of these is a use of friction? (1 mark)
   A. Brakes stopping a bicycle
   B. Wasting energy
   C. Machines wearing out
   D. Making parts hot

30. Why do we put oil on machine parts? (1 mark)
   A. To make them weak
   B. To increase friction
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make them heavy

31. Which of these shows that friction produces heat? (1 mark)
   A. Pouring water
   B. Looking at a torch
   C. Rubbing hands together
   D. Drawing with chalk

32. How does light travel? (1 mark)
   A. In circles
   B. In curves only
   C. In straight lines
   D. In zigzags

33. What is a transparent material? (1 mark)
   A. A material that is always red
   B. A material that blocks all light
   C. A material that lets almost all light pass through
   D. A material that makes light

34. Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. A kettle
   B. The sun
   C. An iron
   D. A fire

35. Which of these is a use of heat? (1 mark)
   A. Hearing sound
   B. Making shadows
   C. Cooking food
   D. Making light only

36. Why should electric irons be unplugged after use? (1 mark)
   A. To prevent burns and fire
   B. To make them hot
   C. To make them noisy
   D. To make them heavier

37. Which of these sources of heat uses electricity? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. Charcoal jiko
   C. Electric iron
   D. Firewood

38. Why are cooking pots made of metal? (1 mark)
   A. Metal is light
   B. Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   C. Metal is soft
   D. Metal does not get hot

39. Which instrument measures temperature? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Thermometer
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Balance

40. What is evaporation? (1 mark)
   A. Liquid water turning into a gas
   B. Water freezing
   C. Water becoming a solid
   D. Water being poured

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango. (5 marks)

42. Explain how drip irrigation and mulching save water. (4 marks)

43. Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

44. Give two effects of force on objects. (2 marks)

45. Describe safety measures to be observed when handling heat at home and at school. (5 marks)

46. Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat. (3 marks)

47. Explain why cooking pots are made of metal but their handles are not. (4 marks)

48. Explain the difference between heat and temperature. (4 marks)

49. Give two ways of reducing waste at home. (2 marks)

50. Describe how you would do an activity to show gravity. (4 marks)

51. Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods. (5 marks)

52. State two uses of light. (2 marks)

53. Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light. (4 marks)

54. Explain why steam from a kettle is invisible although we see a white cloud above the spout. Say what state of matter the cloud is. (5 marks)

55. Explain the importance of conserving water at home and school. (5 marks)

56. Describe how you can show that rough surfaces give more friction than smooth ones. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   Dead plants decay and give nutrients back to the soil.

2. D — Store food
   These roots store food for the plant.

3. D — A drawing app
   A drawing app can be used to draw and label plant parts.

4. A — Seed, root, shoot with leaves
   The seed starts, a root comes out, then a shoot with leaves.

5. B — A plastic flower
   A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

6. C — Water and food
   The stem carries water and mineral salts up and food made in leaves to other parts.

7. C — To get energy and to grow
   Food gives animals energy and materials for growth.

8. A — Butterfly
   A butterfly has six legs and three body parts.

9. D — Eight
   Spiders have eight legs.

10. B — Goat
   Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

11. A — Lungs
   Lungs are for breathing.

12. B — Tell an adult and see a health worker
   Adults and health workers can help find the cause.

13. D — 250 ml
   A cup holds about 250 ml.

14. C — Water
   Water is a liquid.

15. A — Water
   Water can be ice, liquid water or steam.

16. B — The air in a balloon
   Air is a mixture of gases.

17. D — Light from a torch
   Light has no mass and takes up no space.

18. A — Gas
   Cooking gas is a gas that burns to give heat.

19. A — We breathe air
   Air gives us oxygen for breathing.

20. D — Anything that has mass and takes up space
   Matter has mass and occupies space.

21. D — Vegetable peelings
   Vegetable peelings are decomposable.

22. C — Provide bins and clean after the event
   Bins and cleaning keep the place tidy.

23. A — Using a washed bottle to carry water
   The bottle is used again for a new purpose.

24. A — They attract flies and rats that spread diseases
   Flies and rats carry germs.

25. A — It reduces evaporation from the soil
   Covered soil stays moist longer.

26. B — It reduces the water bill
   Less water used means less money paid.

27. C — Less water for others
   Wasted water is not available to others.

28. B — A gutter and a tank
   Gutters carry rain to a tank.

29. A — Brakes stopping a bicycle
   Brakes use friction to slow wheels.

30. C — To reduce friction
   Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

31. C — Rubbing hands together
   Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

32. C — In straight lines
   Light travels in straight lines.

33. C — A material that lets almost all light pass through
   Transparent materials let us see clearly through them.

34. B — The sun
   The sun heats the Earth.

35. C — Cooking food
   Heat cooks food.

36. A — To prevent burns and fire
   Switching off prevents accidents.

37. C — Electric iron
   An electric iron uses electricity.

38. B — Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   Metal passes heat from the fire to the food.

39. B — Thermometer
   A thermometer shows how hot something is.

40. A — Liquid water turning into a gas
   Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drip irrigation sends water drop by drop to the roots so little is lost. Mulch covers soil so less water evaporates.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each method.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Do not play with matches, keep children from fires, use gloves, turn handles inwards, switch off cookers and irons, keep fuels away from fire, cool burns with water and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure up to 5.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Metal passes heat quickly to the food so it cooks. Handles made of wood or plastic pass heat slowly so our hands do not burn.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the pot and 2 marks for the handle.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat is energy that makes things hot. Temperature is how hot something is and it is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for heat and 2 marks for temperature.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drop a stone and a ball from the same height. Observe that they fall down to the ground. Gravity pulls them down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for items, 1 mark for dropping, 1 mark for observing downward fall, 1 mark for conclusion.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Steam is water as a gas and it is invisible. The white cloud is made of tiny water drops which are liquid.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for steam is a gas, 1 mark for invisible, 1 mark for white cloud being tiny drops, 1 mark for liquid, 1 mark for a clear explanation.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: There is enough water for all, we save money, animals and crops get water, it reduces work of fetching water and protects sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason up to 5.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Slide the same block down a ramp covered with different surfaces. It travels a shorter distance on rough surfaces than on smooth ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for method, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.
